# Issue317 generic-QFT addition and ordinary implementation contract

The raw first twenty-criterion packet stays unchanged. The new API snapshots
retain the subsequent four generic-QFT criteria,24 total; all remain open.
`audit.json` verifies the exact original prefix/criterion text and111Issue scope.
`provenance.json` records actual reads and authentication limits. These are
ordinary design records, not constitutional acts or completed implementation.

`checkpoint-proposal.first.md.txt` preserves the draft before its prose-format
repair; `files.before-draft-format.json` preserves that initial mapping, whose
original checkpoint bytes are now available in the first snapshot. The actual
first document-check diagnostic is transcribed in `draft-format-review.json`.
The repaired draft avoids an inline call being interpreted as a local Markdown
link; the mathematical proposal is unchanged. No checker exemption was added.

`before-code-contract.md` is the subsequently reviewed ordinary contract,
posted to317 before the next source experiment. It includes F0 as exact typed
+1 identity, independent small Fourier contracts, an explicit generic common
frontend prerequisite, all current targeted API dispositions and migration.
Raw post-update bodies and `contract-updates.json` bind exact readbacks;152's
original twelve criteria/0.4.0 target remain intact. A local source experiment
cannot establish canonical std availability or close any of317's24 criteria.

`tracker-replacements.json` contains reviewed exact active-scope replacements;
its captured draft status does not assert they have been applied. Historical
performed-results counts and original issue criteria are preserved.
`files.json` binds the final actual bytes and excludes itself. A hash is no
proof, authentication, human judgment or release approval.
